title: Conformance vector vocabulary
description: The complete, fixed vocabulary every vector file is written in. Nothing here requires a language-specific expression evaluator: a per-SDK adapter is a lookup table of subjects plus a switch over six predicates.

case_shape.id: unique within its file; stable across contract versions so a failure is greppable
case_shape.subject: a key of /subjects; may be set per file (default_subject) and overridden per case
case_shape.input: an object matching the subject's input shape
case_shape.why: optional. Present only where the case exists because of a named hazard; carries that hazard's id
case_shape.optional: optional boolean. When true, an adapter that has not registered the subject skips the case instead of failing

assertion_shape.path: a JSON Pointer into the subject's result. The empty string addresses the whole result. Omitted where the predicate takes no path
assertion_shape.value: the expected value; the predicate defines its type

equals.semantics: The value at path is deeply equal to value. Scalars compare by value and type; arrays compare element-wise and in order; null is distinct from absent. No coercion: the string "5" never equals the number 5.

byteLength.semantics: The value at path is a string whose UTF-8 encoding is exactly value bytes long. Not code units, not code points.

matches.semantics: The value at path is a string matched by the regular expression in value.
matches.regex_dialect: The common subset of ECMAScript and RE2: literal characters, character classes, alternation, grouping, the quantifiers * + ? {m} {m,n}, the anchors ^ and $, and backslash escapes. No backreferences, no lookaround, no named groups, no inline flags. ^ and $ mean start and end of the whole string, never of a line. Non-ASCII characters appear as literals, never as escapes or property classes.

isErrorClass.semantics: The subject threw (or rejected with) an error whose contract class name is value. The mapping from a contract class name to a language type is the adapter's job. Implies the subject did not return normally.

rejects.semantics: The subject threw or rejected. Use with isErrorClass to pin which error.

throwsNothing.semantics: The subject returned normally. Present on cases where not throwing is the point, not merely incidental.

part_forms: { "repeat": "<string>", "times": <integer> } — the string concatenated with itself times times
byte_string.semantics: Parts are concatenated in order and the result is encoded as UTF-8. The generative form keeps a ten-kilobyte fixture readable and diffable; a base64 blob would not be.
byte_string.empty: An empty parts array denotes the empty string.

instant.shape: an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit Z offset
instant.semantics: The clock reading the subject must treat as 'now'. Every time-dependent subject takes its clock as input; no vector reads a real clock.

input.action: string or null — the raw, percent-decoded path segment after the monitor id; null means no segment

result.routable: boolean — whether the server's route pattern accepts this segment at all
result.kind: string or null — the ping kind the server records; null when the request never reaches the mapper
result.mapperKind: string — what the action mapper alone would return, ignoring routing. Always populated, so the mapper's behaviour on unroutable input stays pinned

ping.classifyAction.note: This models the server; it is not a function an SDK calls on a hot path. Implement it in test scope if that is cheaper than exporting it.

ping.assertEmittableAction.note: The wiring-time guard. The emittable set is exactly null, "start", "success", "fail" — canonical lowercase only. It is deliberately narrower than what the server accepts: the moment an SDK accepts a variable here, a typo becomes a silent success report.

input.status: integer — the HTTP status of the ping response
input.body: string — the response body as text; the empty string when there was none

result.outcome: string — a member of the ping.outcome vocabulary
result.ok: boolean — whether the server recorded the check-in

ping.classifyResponse.note: Every row of /ping/responses/table is covered by a case in this group, and an SDK-side test asserts that, so a row nobody classifies fails rather than going unnoticed.

body.truncate.result: string — the body as it will be sent

input.status: integer — the HTTP status of a management-API response
input.detail: string or null — the problem document's detail field, present only so that cases can vary it and assert the classification does not move
input.deliversDownstream: optional boolean — whether the route delivers to a destination the caller owns. Only the channel-test route does, and only there does a 502 mean the destination failed rather than the API

api.classifyStatus.result: throws the classified error; never returns
api.classifyStatus.note: The classification reads the status and the route, and nothing else. There is no machine-readable code on a problem response, so a port that branched on detail would be branching on English prose that a server-side rewording silently changes.

input.header: string or null — the raw header value

runner_requirements: Every file's contract_version must equal the version of the contract the SDK was built against; a mismatch fails the suite rather than being tolerated.
An unknown predicate fails the suite. Silently skipping one would make the harness vacuously green.
An unknown subject fails the suite unless the case carries optional: true.
The runner asserts the total case count it executed against the count in the files, so a filtering bug cannot hide as a pass.
